text.en: Why is the plural of mouse mice but the plural of house not hice?

This light-hearted poem plays with the odd rules of English. It points out irregular plurals such as mouse and mice, goose and geese, man and men, foot and feet, tooth and teeth, and asks why booth is not beeth or boot not beet.
The poem teaches that English has many exceptions, so we should learn irregular forms carefully and enjoy the language's quirks. It also shows how rhyme and humour make grammar memorable.
Grammar focus: irregular plurals. Regular plurals add s or es; irregular ones change the word or stay the same. Compare house and houses with mouse and mice.
